facts: Some auction domains have uncertainty regarding the final availability of the goods being auctioned off.
A government may auction off spectrum from its public safety network.
Spectrum may be needed back in times of emergency.
In auction domains with uncertainty regarding the final availability of the goods being auctioned off, standard combinatorial auctions perform poorly.
Standard combinatorial auctions lead to violations of individual rationality (IR) even in expectation.
The paper studies the design of core-selecting payment rules for auction domains with uncertainty regarding the final availability of the goods being auctioned off.
In auction domains with uncertainty regarding the final availability of the goods being auctioned off, there does not exist a payment rule guaranteed to be ex-post core-selecting.
Execution-contingent rules can reduce violations of individual rationality (IR).
Execution-contingent rules charge payments that are conditioned on the realization of the availability of the goods.
The paper designs two core-selecting rules that always satisfy IR in expectation.
The paper performs a computational Bayes-Nash equilibrium analysis to study the performance of the rules.
In equilibrium, the core-selecting rules designed in the paper have better incentives than standard core-selecting rules.
In equilibrium, the core-selecting rules designed in the paper have higher efficiency than standard core-selecting rules.
In equilibrium, the core-selecting rules designed in the paper have a lower rate of ex-post IR violations than standard core-selecting rules.
